rounds.text: SC Agrotech Ltd trades at a modest P/E ratio of 11.8x [E1] alongside an intrinsic value assessment of ₹ 123 per share derived from a discounted cash flow model, leaving a substantial margin of safety of 71.1% [E42, E43]. The market price of ₹ 35.6 [E2] drastically underappreciates the extraordinary fundamental momentum, evidenced by a trailing twelve month sales growth of 2191% [E17] and a staggering 5348% compounded profit growth over the same period [E21]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF demonstrates that the current share price prices in a negligible 0.9% earnings growth against a base case assumption of 18.0% [E44], highlighting a profound disconnect between valuation and underlying operating reality. Profit growth has heavily outpaced share price performance, with 5-year profit growth reaching 142% compared to a mere 23% share price appreciation [E23, E45, E49], while the company maintains an exceptionally clean balance sheet with a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.07x [E37] and strong margin expansion driven by a TTM operating margin of 19% [E30]. Conceded: promoters hold 0.00% as of Sep 2026 down from 39.43% in Dec 2023 [E40], operating cash flow is negative at Rs -107 Cr for Mar 2026 [E35], and the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4].

Despite recent explosive top-line growth, SC Agrotech Ltd carries severe fundamental risks highlighted by a complete desertion of management and insiders, with promoter holding crashing from 39.43% in December 2023 down to 0.00% by September 2026 [E40]. This alarming absence of skin in the game is compounded by atrocious capital efficiency, evidenced by a 3-year median return on equity of just 3% [E28] and a multi-year trend of depressed profitability [E26, E27]. The company's reported earnings fail to translate into actual liquidity, demonstrated by a catastrophic operating cash flow and free cash flow of negative Rs 107 Cr each for March 2026, leading to a negative cash conversion ratio of -35.67x against reported profit [E34, E35, E36]. Operational health is further undermined by high debtors stretching to 225 days [E52], an inconsistent operating-margin trend [E32, E33], and a mounting borrowing burden of Rs 10 Cr up from zero a year prior [E38]. Conceded: the business shows robust historical compounded sales and profit growth over multiple periods alongside a conservative current debt-to-equity ratio [E14, E15, E16, E17, E18, E19, E20, E21, E37].

Conceded: promoter holding fell to 0.00% [E40], and operating cash flow was negative Rs 107 Cr [E35]. However, the bear's focus on historical median ROE overlooks that recent fundamentals are vastly superior, with TTM operating margins expanding to 19% and quarterly margins hitting 30% [E30, E31]. The market is ignoring this fundamental acceleration, as evidenced by a reverse DCF showing today's price implies a negligible 0.9% earnings growth rate despite historical profit compounding at 142% over five years and 5348% in the trailing twelve months [E21, E44, E49]. Debt remains minimal at a 0.07x debt-to-equity ratio [E37], completely undermining the narrative of a mounting borrowing burden from a nominal Rs 10 Cr level [E38]. Furthermore, intrinsic valuation models place fair value far above the current market price of ₹ 35.6, offering a substantial 71.1% margin of safety that more than compensates for reported debtor days [E42, E43, E52].

Conceded: the reverse DCF implies a growth rate of 0.9% and the debt-to-equity ratio sits at a low 0.07x [E44, E37]. However, dismissing the collapse of promoter holding to 0.00% as a minor detail ignores a complete exodus of insiders who once held 39.43% [E40]. While recent margin expansion is highlighted, it accompanies an alarming cash conversion ratio of -35.67x driven by a staggering negative operating and free cash flow of Rs -107 Cr [E34, E35, E36]. Furthermore, pointing to multi-year profit compounding fails to reconcile with severely depressed long-term returns, evidenced by a 10-year median ROE of just 2% and a recent 3-year average of 2.76% [E26, E51]. The reliance on a theoretical margin of safety glosses over the operational reality of high debtors stretching to 225 days alongside a zero dividend yield [E43, E50, E52].
